blurb: How to turn a mattress safely: share the load, use good technique and stop if you feel strain.

cards.title: Manual Handling — Flipping & Turning Mattresses
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- explain why mattresses cause strain
- use safe technique to turn one
- stop and report if you feel strain

cards.title: Heavy, floppy and awkward
cards.body: Turning and flipping mattresses is a routine part of keeping rooms in top condition, but it is a sneaky cause of back, shoulder and wrist strain. Mattresses are heavy, floppy and awkward to grip. A little technique goes a long way.

cards.title: Share it and clear the space
cards.body: Wherever possible, make it a two-person job. One person wrestling with a mattress alone is asking for a pulled muscle. Clear the area around the bed so you do not trip or knock into furniture.

cards.title: Stages, not one big lift
cards.body: Do not try to lift the whole dead weight in one go. Push, roll and turn it in stages, and let the bed take the weight.

items.title: Turn
items.text: Move your feet, do not twist.

items.title: Lower
items.text: Let the bed take the weight.

cards.title: Stop and get help
cards.body:
If you feel any strain or a twinge, stop. Do not push through it. Report it and get help before carrying on.

> Never feel you have to struggle on alone to save time.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Make it a two-person job
- Clear the area first
- Knees bent, back straight, move your feet, never twist
- Push, roll and turn in stages
- Stop and report any strain

cards.q: What's the safest way to turn a mattress?
cards.why: Two people sharing the load can turn a mattress smoothly and safely.

cards.q: You should keep your back straight and bend your knees.
cards.why: Good lifting basics: firm grip, bend your knees, keep your back straight.

cards.q: To change direction while turning a mattress you should…
cards.why: Move your feet to turn rather than twisting your spine.

cards.q: You should try to lift the whole mattress dead-weight in one go.
cards.why: Push, roll and turn it in stages and let the bed take the weight.

cards.q: What should you do to the area around the bed before you start?
options: Move the bed away from the wall
cards.why: Clear the area so you do not trip or knock into furniture as you move.

cards.q: If you feel a strain, you should push through and finish the job.
cards.why: Stop, report it and get help before carrying on.

cards.q: Turning a mattress is best done by…
options: Pushing, rolling and turning in stages
Lifting it all in one go
cards.why: Working in stages lets the bed take the weight.

cards.q: Using the mattress handles (if fitted) helps you get a safe grip.
cards.why: A firm grip is part of the basics, using the handles if the mattress has them.

cards.q: Name one part of the body commonly strained by poor mattress handling.
cards.why: Back, shoulder and wrist strain are the common injuries from mattress handling.

cards.q: You should never feel you have to struggle on alone to save time.
cards.why: Heavy, awkward tasks are far safer shared. Looking after your body keeps you able to do the job.
